name: Account & identity pivoting
description: Turn one account or handle into the person's other accounts, and know when a shared username is NOT the same person.
author: vineyard-run
overview:
Account & identity pivoting — from one handle or email to the accounts behind the same person, without over-merging strangers who happen to share a name.

Use this when the analyst has a username, email, or profile and wants "where else is this person". Load a section:
  - "handles"  — spreading from one username across platforms
  - "corroborate" — what actually ties two accounts to ONE person (and what doesn't)

Read "corroborate" first: the whole risk here is collapsing two people into one node.

sections.summary: Spreading from one username across platforms.
sections.body:
From a USERNAME:
- Run the account-search plugin (WhatsMyName) to enumerate the handle across ~700 sites. Each hit is a CANDIDATE account node — not yet the same person.
- Look for the handle reused in email local-parts, vanity URLs, and display names.
- A rare, distinctive handle reused verbatim is a strong lead; a common word as a handle is weak (many unrelated people pick it).

Model each found account as its own node with its own platform — never collapse "@alice on GitHub" and "@alice on Telegram" into one username node. They share a username and are different accounts until something corroborates one owner (see "corroborate"). Stage a node per account and hold the "same person" edge until you have that evidence.

sections.summary: What actually ties two accounts to one person — and what doesn't.
sections.body:
Same username is a LEAD, not proof of one person. Corroborate before drawing a "same person" / "controls" edge:

Strong: a shared verified email or phone; one account linking to the other; identical rare bio text / avatar hash reused; a password-reset or profile field that ties them.
Weak / not proof: the same common handle; the same city; following each other; similar posting times.

When you have real corroboration, stage the link with a label for the EVIDENCE ("shares recovery email", "cross-links to"), not the conclusion ("is"). When you do not, say the accounts are candidates for the same person and hand the judgement to the analyst — do not assert identity from a shared handle. Every node and edge is staged for their review; a wrong merge is the most damaging thing you can propose here.
